text:
mike: Heads-up — NovaRetail expects a presales POC: streaming with reconnect/resume, function-calls that fan out to customer webhooks, and bounded batching (tail latency <150ms). Security + pricing flagged as blockers. Can eng ops + SDK folks confirm feasibility and a short runbook?

anya: we can support reconnect in SDKs. pattern = session id + resume-index + idempotency key for tool calls. default resume window for hosted POC is 30s. can extend on Dedicated. :+1:

devon: SDK details: node/go/python have reconnect hooks but we need to show an example. also confirm structured-output schema for webhook payloads — best if they provide a jsonschema for validation.

mike: they will provide schema but want example payloads and how we pass outputs to tool-calls. also worried about duplicated webhook side-effects on resume.

rachel: recommend including an "x-redwood-call-id" on each tool call and require webhook to be idempotent. if they can't change webhooks, we can enable an internal call-log in Dedicated to dedupe on replay.

legal-bot: Q from NovaRetail security questionnaire: do resumed-session blobs contain customer data? retention window? KMS details?

anya: short answers we can give: hosted resume blobs do not store plaintext prompts — we persist KV-deltas and token indices plus HMAC/checksum. blobs encrypted with envelope keys in our KMS. TTL enforced (default 30s for POC), audit logs for resume blob access. Dedicated/private customers can use customer-managed KMS.

ops-bot: canary report: resume-state feature deployed to staging-poc; reconnect->resume success 97% under 50 concurrent streams, median resume latency 12ms.

devon: sample client reconnect (HTTP/WS header example):

```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Redwood-Session: novaretail-7a2
X-Redwood-Resume-Index: 892
X-Redwood-Call-Id: call_2026_0001
```

Node sample (simplified):

```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
    'X-Redwood-Session': sessionId,
    'X-Redwood-Resume-Index': lastIndex,
    'X-Redwood-Call-Id': callId
  }
});
// stream handling and resume logic handled by SDK
```

devon: note on tool-calls + structured output: if a tool-call happened at token index 892 and client reconnects at 900, we do not re-run the webhook by default. the SDK/runtime returns the same structured output chunk and the client should check call_id to decide.

mike: pricing ask: POC estimate = 2 weeks, expected 500k tokens, traffic spikes up to 2k concurrent streams for short bursts. how to price/guarantee?

anya: hosted: bill per-token as usual. resumed tokens already accounted for if we don't re-generate; duplicates only billed if model re-generation occurs. suggest offering a POC credit covering up to 1.1x tokens for the trial to cover replays. Dedicated: reserved capacity to meet tail-latency SLOs, pricing via monthly commit.

rachel: record for security questionnaire: provide brief paragraph on encryption, retention, access controls, and optional customer-managed KMS. I'll draft language.

mike: next steps: 1) devon/anya — put a 1-pager + code snippets for node+go (short) 2) operations — confirm staging perf and dedicated TTL/redis plan 3) legal — draft security answers 4) I'll share pricing proposal with NovaRetail this afternoon.

anya: will prepare the 1-pager + SDK snippets and include a clear note about idempotency and call-id.

devon: will add a minimal Go snippet and a small section on structured-output validation and tool-call checkpointing.

rachel: drafting security Q answers now, will ping legal for review. :eyes:

mike: awesome, thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer once docs + pricing are ready. :rocket:
